newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka urged to ignore "sensitive" links to killing.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka urged to ignore "sensitive" links to killing.

text.p: Bangladesh's government, preparing to try the accused killers of independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, should tread cautiously in prosecuting the case, Bangladeshi intelligence officers said on Wednesday.
The officers, who asked not to be identified, said the advice was given to the government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, Mujib's daughter. Mujib was killed in a 1975 military coup.
The officers said the government should seek to put on trial only those suspected of direct involvement in the killing.
"But trying to punish others involved in the plot to kill Mujib could be too sensitive and dangerous to touch upon," a high-level intelligence source said.

"Such a move could lead to many surprises and expose heavyweight political and diplomatic connections. Taking them to trial might upset the country's current delicate political balance," the source said without elaborating.
Government officials were not immediately available to comment.
Mujib, who led Bangladesh to independence from Pakistan in 1971, was killed with most members of his family on August 15, 1975, in the nation's first army revolt.
Hasina took over as prime minister following a general election in June that returned Mujib's Awami League to power 21 years after his death.
Hasina is seeking to repeal soon a 1975 ordinance that gave Mujib's killers indemnity from law, sources in her party said.
In the meantime, police have started a formal investigation into the killing, and have already arrested three former army officers and Mujib's information minister Taheruddin Thakur.
They all are being interrogated, police said.
The three are retired Colonels Farook Reehman and Shahriar Rashid Khan, and retired Major Mohammad Khairuzzaman.
Police were also looking for several other former army officers believed involved in Mujib's death and the killing of four Awami leaders in the Dhaka Central Jail in November, 1975.

The Dhaka daily Bhorer Kagoj said on Wednesday the government had appointed a high-level task force headed by Home (Interior) Minister Rafiqul Islam to work out plans to bring home Mujib's killers now staying abroad.
The newspaper report was confirmed by the intelligence officers.
The government says six suspected killers were assigned to diplomatic posts abroad after the 1975 coup.
